**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The licence architecture here runs in our favour:

- **§13.3(a)** grants MSL only a narrow royalty-free right to use IBM confidential information "necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM," with any broader licence requiring a separate signed IBM agreement.
- **§24.1(a)** and the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement **§5 (Ownership and License)** and **§6 (Licensed Internal Code)** are likewise IBM→MSL grants, tightly scoped to MSL's authorized use. These restrictions benefit our side, so they are not flagged.
- **§13.1** puts us above the preferred position: IBM takes ownership and MSL assigns all IP in Products, plus MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes, and MSL may not use proprietary processes for the Products without written agreement. We therefore hold ownership, not a revocable licence — there is no grant to IBM that MSL can revoke at will or that excludes our affiliates/contractors, so the walk-away scenario does not arise.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: there is no IBM affiliate/"Related Company" extension (the concept is used only for MSL), and no express licence-back of MSL background IP for transition to a replacement manufacturer. Successor/transfer mechanics sit in §16.2 and §16.5 (MSL warrants any acquirer assumes performance) and belong to the assignment rule rather than being double-flagged here.
